Report each length-match group: every net's routed length and delay, how far each falls short of the longest net, the spread, and whether the group is inside its tolerance; read only
Report routed copper length per net: track segments summed in millimetres, with via counts and unrouted nets listed
Rename an existing net; the new name must be unique
Set a target routed length and tolerance for one net, or clear the target by omitting it; nets in a class follow their own target when they have one
Exchange the names of two nets; each net keeps its id, members and copper, so two nets that crossed during a reassignment can be corrected in one step
Merge two nets into one: every pin, wire, label, track, via and zone on the source net joins the target net, net class and clearance pair memberships follow, and the source net is removed
Rip up the routed copper of one net: every track and via carrying that net leaves the board in a single undo step, while the net, its pads and its unrouted connection stay
Create a net class with a clearance requirement, a default track width and optional member nets
Move a net into a net class, or out of every class when the class is null
Move every net whose name matches a wildcard pattern into a net class in one step; * matches any run of characters and ? matches one

pattern.description: case-sensitive name pattern, must contain * or ?

commands.description: Change the clearance a net class requires between its copper and everything else
Set the target routed length and tolerance a net class demands; omitted values stay as they were
Delete a net class and return its nets to the board default rules
Rename a net class, change routing defaults, via size, or differential-pair defaults, with the class rules echoed back
Set the longest dead-end copper branch a net class allows; null clears the limit
Set the smallest and largest track width a net class allows; omitted bounds stay as they were
Export the connectivity table: every net with its pins by reference, plus unconnected pins
Import a netlist table: assign listed pins to named nets by reference, creating missing nets
Import net assignments from a Specctra session file on disk: every named net with pins is created if missing and its REF-PIN entries are assigned to matching component pins
Delete a component, wire, track, via, zone, footprint, cutout or unused net by stable ID
Duplicate components at an offset, each with a fresh reference and ids, bringing its footprint when one exists
Slide one placed board object, track, via, footprint, zone, cutout or text label, by a distance in millimetres
Snap component or footprint placements to the nearest multiple of a grid

Record a named fabrication output recipe listing export kinds (gerbers, netlist, bom, placement, dxf, cmp, idf, vrml, step, pdf, svg, ipc2581, dsn, ipc356, gencad, hyperlynx, plot, report, ps, odb, hpgl, stackup, drill chart, board statistics, uv_print for silkscreen artwork for a UV printer) that can be re-run after any edit

Write a whole fabrication bundle as one zip file: gerbers and drill files for every layer, the bill of materials and the pick-and-place file, plus a manifest that names every file with its size, checksum, export kind and the job that produced it. Name a recorded output job to package its recipe, or a list of kinds, or nothing for the fabrication bundle
Remove a recorded output job by name
Run an output job: write every file of its recipe (fabrication layers, netlist, bill of materials, placement, drawing) into a directory in one step

uv_print.description: Settings for a uv_print kind: silkscreen artwork for a UV printer. Defaults to the top side at 720 DPI with 0.3 mm bleed.

commands.description: Report every board pad: number, net, position, shape, size and drill, by component reference
Define or replace a named reusable pad shape: copper shape and size with an optional drill, ready for any placed pad to adopt

drill.description: drill diameter, millimetres; omit for a surface pad

commands.description: Copy a defined padstack under a fresh name, same copper and drill, ready to reshape other pads without touching the original
Remove a named padstack from the design; pads already shaped by it keep their copper
Rename a defined padstack in place; pads already shaped by it keep their copper, and the new name must still be free
Report every defined padstack with its copper and drill, which placed pads carry it, and which stacks no pad uses, so unused stacks can be tidied away; reads the design without touching it
Turn off panel settings and return them to defaults
Write panel fabrication files (duplicated gerbers, drill with breakaway and tooling holes, pick-and-place per copy) into a directory
Record manufacturing panel settings on the project: grid size, gaps, rails, tab channel width and separation method
List the project's named numeric parameters with their values, notes and the object fields that follow each one
Forget a named parameter; while objects still follow it the call is refused and names them, unless unbind is set to release them first

Record a named numeric parameter, or change one, and re-run the commands that reference it: holes and vias whose size or position follows the name are written again inside the same undoable step, and a value that breaks one of them is refused and changes nothing. Names are 1 to 32 letters, digits or underscores starting with a letter or underscore

Record where a part came from on a placed component in one step: manufacturer, part number, datasheet link and the distributor's own order number are written as named properties (Manufacturer, MPN, Datasheet, and one property per distributor ending in SKU)
Step and repeat holes and cutouts into a grid: every named object is copied at each column and row offset, row by row, and each copy is an independent object
Mark a pin intentionally unconnected, suppressing its unconnected-pin violation
Remove every no-connect flag of one component in a single undo step
Flag every pin of one component that is neither wired nor assigned, in a single undo step; pins already flagged are skipped
Write the NeoDen YY1 placement file for one or both sides and the feeder sheet into a folder, using a pick and place machine profile recorded on the design. Reads the design and records nothing

Plot the copper of one layer onto the schematic as editable drawing graphics (tracks become lines, vias become circles and board text joins the plot), shifted so the board origin lands on a chosen sheet point; the copper itself is untouched

include_text.description: also plot board text of that layer, default true

layer.description: copper layer name for the current stackup

commands.description: Remove one project metadata entry by key
Write the whole design, including its attached text files, to a self-contained archive file that a colleague can open without any other project files
Open a self-contained archive file written by the export, replacing the current project; the replacement is undoable
Rename the current project

Find text across the project and replace it in one call: component references, values and fields, net names, free board and schematic text, and graphic text; a dry run reports every hit without changing anything
Record a project metadata entry such as title, revision, company or notes, keyed by 1 to 32 lowercase alphanumeric bytes; recording the same value again is refused

Record the unit this design is read in: millimetres, mils or inches. Stored coordinates stay millimetres; inch drill and gerber fabrication output converts to inches, and the recorded unit is reported in the board statistics

Show an attached PNG under the schematic or the board for tracing. Position is the top-left corner in millimetres, scale is millimetres per pixel. Reference pictures are editor-only and never reach any export
Remove a reference picture; the attached file stays
Move, rescale, fade or hide a reference picture

Add a rectangular rule area that demands a stricter minimum copper separation for copper whose midpoints lie inside it; optionally narrowed to one net and one copper layer, which apply when either side of a pair matches

clearance.description: minimum separation inside the area, in millimetres

keepout.description: true keeps all copper and tracks at least the clearance away from the rectangle

layer.description: copper layer name for the current stackup

max_height.description: optional maximum component height inside the area, in millimetres

commands.description: Remove one rule area by id
Give a rule area a maximum component height, in millimetres, for boards that must fit under a cover; send height as null to clear the restriction and keep only the clearance

height.description: maximum component height in millimetres, or null to clear

commands.description: Remove the clearance override between two net classes
Require a minimum clearance between two net classes, stricter than either class alone
Silence one check code for particular design objects; a finding drops when every object it names is excluded

code.description: check code, as listed by rules.severity

ids.description: component, net, track, via, zone, cutout, wire or footprint ids to exempt

commands.description: Silence one check code inside a rectangle; a finding drops when every object it names sits within the region

code.description: check code, as listed by rules.severity

commands.description: Lift object exclusions for one check code; omit ids to lift every exclusion of that code
Lift rectangular region exclusions for one check code; omit index to lift every region of that code

index.description: which region of that code to remove, oldest first; omit to remove all

commands.description: Apply a named fabrication capability preset to the board rules in one undo step
List the built-in fabrication capability presets
Apply a built-in profile by id or a profile TOML file from disk; optional dry run returns the plan without changing the design

nets_override.description: only assign nets in this list

commands.description: List built-in interface rule profiles with id, name, category and summary
Change how one check code reports: error, warning, or off to silence it; null or omitting severity restores its default

code.description: check code: unassigned_pin, single_pin_net, clearance, copper_short, pad_clearance_bound, board_edge, cutout_clearance, track_width, track_length, stub_length, unrouted, missing_footprint, panel_copper_near_score, panel_component_near_score, panel_tab_too_narrow, panel_too_large_for_assembler, panel_missing_fiducials

commands.description: Tidy the schematic in one undoable step: merge junctions that repeat the same net at the same point, drop vertices where a wire repeats itself or runs straight through, and leave any vertex a junction still depends on exactly where it is

Import a sheet file from disk as a new schematic page: components built from the built-in symbol templates with their positions, rotations and properties, and hierarchy ports that join existing nets by name
Move a component to another schematic page, sheet 0 being the root page; its position never changes
Move a hierarchy port to another position, another page, or both at once; a port moved onto a page that already carries its name is refused
Add a named schematic page; every component lives on exactly one page and sheet 0 is the root page every design starts with
Place a named hierarchy port for a net on a schematic page; a port name already used on another page must carry the same net, which is how a net is handed between pages
Remove a hierarchy port; the net itself is untouched
Remove a schematic page; while the page still holds components a move_to destination (another page or the root page 0) is required, and the components keep their positions when they move
Rename a hierarchy port so a page hands its net under a better name; the net travels with the port, and a new name already used on the same page or carrying a different net on another page is refused
Rename a schematic page; the new name must differ from every other page name

Draw a parts table on the schematic at a position: one row per component sorted by reference, one column per property key (reference and value by default), as ordinary graphics that capture the design as it stands now
Serialize a bounded selection to the versioned text clipboard form
Paste a text clipboard selection at an offset, renumbering references when asked and matching nets by name

Import an SVG drawing from disk as board graphics (lines, polylines, polygons, rectangles, circles, simple paths and text, in millimetres with the page flipping y up); with use_outline a closed polygon also traces the board outline and the whole drawing shifts to the first quadrant

Re-read a symbol from its library file and refresh every placed component that carries it, in one undo step, so symbol artwork and pin geometry edits propagate; components whose pin numbers or units no longer match are skipped and reported

path.description: symbol library file, nickname paths allowed

commands.description: Grow teardrop copper where tracks meet pads and vias so junctions survive etching and hand soldering; filter by net or layer, and junctions that already have a teardrop are left alone

depth.description: how far the teardrop runs along the track from the junction, millimetres; default 0.5

layer.description: copper layer name for the current stackup

commands.description: Take teardrop copper away again from every junction it was grown on, optionally filtered by net or layer

layer.description: copper layer name for the current stackup

commands.description: Bind a board text to a component so drawings resolve its ${REFERENCE}, ${VALUE}, ${FOOTPRINT} and field-key tokens; null detaches it

component.description: component to resolve tokens from; null detaches

commands.description: Write a bound component's values into one board text's ${...} tokens, or every bound text when no id is given; unknown tokens stay
Move a board text label to a new position
Place a text label on the board with a size in millimetres and a layer

layer.description: copper layer name for the current stackup

commands.description: Turn a board text label to an absolute angle in degrees about its anchor
Change a board text label's string, size, layer, or rotation

layer.description: copper layer name for the current stackup

rotation.description: text angle in degrees about the anchor

commands.description: Add a straight copper segment; checks report clearance errors rather than hiding them

layer.description: copper layer name for the current stackup

commands.description: Add a curved copper segment through three points (start, a point on the curve, end); clearance checks sample the arc and fabrication output draws a true arc

layer.description: copper layer name for the current stackup

commands.description: Cut the corner between two joined same-net track segments with a diagonal segment

size.description: distance cut back from the corner along each segment, millimetres

commands.description: Remove dangling track stubs, merge collinear same-net segments on one layer, and drop zero-length pieces in one undo step
Translate an existing copper segment by a delta; both ends move together

Connect a same-net pad or point to another on the chosen copper layer. Default mode orthogonal is one right-angle bend with no obstacle checks. Mode octilinear routes 45-degree copper around other nets' pads, tracks and cutouts. Mode octilinear_shove walks around pads and cutouts and pushes other nets' tracks aside within fixed iteration limits. Refusals say why and change nothing. Single layer, no vias

from.description: A pad (footprint and pad number) or a point on the board in millimetres; a route between two points also needs net

layer.description: copper layer name for the current stackup

to.description: A pad (footprint and pad number) or a point on the board in millimetres; a route between two points also needs net

commands.description: Route both nets of a declared differential pair between two pad pairs on the chosen copper layer with coupled geometry at the pair gap; corners are cut at 45 degrees by default, mode orthogonal keeps right angles

Bend an existing track into a circular arc through a new midpoint, straight or already curved alike; the ends, width, layer and net stay put and only the curve changes, so a routed run can swing around an obstacle without being ripped up and redrawn
Drag one end of an existing track to a new position, shortening, lengthening or re-aiming it; the other end stays put

end.description: which end of the segment to move

commands.description: Move an existing track segment to the other copper layer without moving its ends

layer.description: copper layer name for the current stackup

commands.description: Move every track segment of one net to the other copper layer in a single step, optionally only those currently on a given layer; reports how many segments moved

from_layer.description: only move segments starting on this layer; null moves all of them

layer.description: copper layer name for the current stackup

commands.description: Change the width of an existing track segment
Set the copper width of every track segment on one net in a single step, so a whole net can be thickened or thinned at once; reports how many segments changed
Split one copper segment into two at a point on the track
Turn a curved track back into the straight segment between its ends

Replace one straight track with a serpentine so the net's total routed length reaches a target within a tolerance. Bumps rise on whichever side has room, legs are spaced at least three dielectric heights apart by default and no longer than fifteen heights, corners are 45 degree mitres or rounded. Refuses curved tracks, differential pair nets, nets already at or beyond the target, and runs with no clear room, leaving the design untouched. Reports before and after length and delay

amplitude_max.description: tallest bump, millimetres; default 10, capped at fifteen dielectric heights

spacing.description: edge to edge gap between legs, millimetres; default the larger of three dielectric heights and clearance plus width; a value under three heights is accepted with a warning

target.description: wanted total routed length of the net, millimetres

commands.description: Remove an assembly variant's footprint swap for one component, restoring the footprint the design places
Define a named assembly variant, optionally with a note and an initial set of component ids to leave unpopulated
Delete an assembly variant by name
Set which components an assembly variant leaves unpopulated: with dnp true (default) the listed component ids join the set, with dnp false they leave it; an empty list with dnp true clears the set
Record that an assembly variant populates one component with a different footprint, replacing any earlier swap for that component; a variant bill of materials prints these swaps

footprint.description: package this build uses in place of the placed footprint

commands.description: Replace the note describing what an assembly variant changes, or clear it when the note is null or omitted
Allow or forbid one extra via span on this board, such as a buried span the fabricator offers; forbidding is refused while a via uses the span
Move a placed via to a new position; geometry and net are kept
Place a plated via on an existing net. It joins front and back copper unless from_layer and to_layer limit it to a blind or buried span the board allows; size defaults from the net class when omitted

from_layer.description: upper copper layer of the span, for example F.Cu or In1.Cu; default is the top layer

to_layer.description: lower copper layer of the span; default is the bottom layer

commands.description: Set how one via is protected under the solder mask (open, tented, tented_covered, plugged, plugged_covered, filled, filled_covered, filled_capped, named after the seven via protection types); omit covering to follow the board default. Anything but open needs a drilled hole
Change the pad and drill diameters of an existing via

diameter.description: outer copper pad diameter in millimetres

drill.description: drilled hole diameter in millimetres; keeps the current drill when omitted

commands.description: Change which copper layers an existing via joins, making it through, blind or buried; the span must be one the board allows

from_layer.description: upper copper layer of the span; keeps the current one when omitted

to_layer.description: lower copper layer of the span; keeps the current one when omitted

commands.description: Fill a rectangular area with a grid of stitched vias on an existing net
Insert a vertex into a drawn wire at any position along it, extending either end

index.description: vertex position the new point takes

commands.description: Connect two pins; infer their existing net or atomically create a net if neither is assigned
Draw a free-form schematic wire with explicit vertices, optionally bound to a net

Draw a multi-net bus wire from explicit vertices and label its first vertex with the bus notation; the name is stem*count, like DB*8 naming DB0 through DB7, and member nets that do not exist yet are created in the same step
Slide a drawn wire by a distance; junctions sitting on its vertices travel with it
Remove one vertex from a drawn wire, shortening it or straightening a corner
Drag one vertex of a drawn wire to a new position, bending or straightening it; refused if a junction would be left off the wire
Split a drawn wire into two at a point on one of its segments
Add a closed cutout outline that removes copper from an existing zone

outline.description: closed polygon, millimetres; first vertex repeated last

commands.description: Report the copper a zone actually pours on its layer: area, connected pieces, thermal spokes that reach the fill, pads left starved, detached islands and how many the settings removed, with knockouts round foreign copper, keepouts and the board edge already applied
Insert a new vertex into a poured zone's outline, or one of its cutouts, at an index; outlines hold 3 to 256 vertices

cutout.description: which cutout outline to edit; omit to edit the zone outline

commands.description: Translate a poured zone by a delta; outline and every cutout move together
Place a poured copper zone: a closed polygon of copper on one layer bound to an existing net

layer.description: copper layer name for the current stackup

outline.description: closed polygon, millimetres; first vertex repeated last

commands.description: Set how a zone pours: whether plated pads and vias join solid, through thermal spokes or not at all, the relief gap, spoke width and count, the narrowest copper it keeps, and whether detached copper is kept or dropped

island_area.description: with remove_below, the area in square millimetres at or above which a detached piece is kept

islands.description: what happens to copper that touches nothing of its net

min_width.description: narrowest copper the pour keeps in millimetres; null follows the narrowest track on the board

pad_connect.description: how plated pads inside the zone join the pour

relief_gap.description: gap round a relieved pad in millimetres

spoke_width.description: width of each thermal spoke in millimetres

spokes.description: spokes per pad, aligned to the pad rotation

via_connect.description: how vias inside the zone join the pour

commands.description: Remove one vertex from a poured zone's outline, or one of its cutouts, by index; at least three vertices must remain

cutout.description: which cutout outline to edit; omit to edit the zone outline

commands.description: Pour a zone's copper back in, or take it out to a bare outline that carries no copper and reports no findings

filled.description: true pours the copper, false leaves only the outline

commands.description: Move a poured zone, with all its cutouts, to the other copper layer without moving its outline

layer.description: copper layer name for the current stackup

commands.description: Re-bind a poured zone to another existing net in place; the outline, cutouts, layer and fill state stay put
Move one vertex of a poured zone's outline, or of one of its cutouts, by index; closing vertices stay paired

cutout.description: which cutout outline to edit; omit to edit the zone outline
